page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; a narrow strip of text at the right edge of the scan belongs to the facing page and is cut off mid-word, so it is a margin of the neighbouring page and is transcribed as notes only where clearly legible. Page number at the head centred.

main_text.l: rum irritamenta, &, uno nomine,
instrumentum est omnis nequitiæ) pos-
sit magnam illius partem citissimè ad has
& illas terræ partes amandare, illa-
que mediante innumera tam in terræ
viscceribus, quàm in ejus superficie
producere.
V.
Firmiter tamen statui posse videtur
malum Genium mente nostra in hoc
inferiorem esse, quòd non pro lubitu
& quoties vult per hæc corpora agere
possit, uti mens nostro si modò illud
sit bene dispositum. Nam ex jam di-
ctis patet, quòd talis nexus naturalis in-
ter quodcunque corpus, & inter malum
Genium non sit, adeoque se toties sol-
um eis jungere queat, quoties Deus
hoc aut jubet eoque utitur, vel tan-
quam carnifice suo & exequutore vo-
luntatis & justitiæ suæ ut homines cru-
ciet, seu quoad corpus solùm, seu
quoad mentem solam, seu quoad u-
trumque, vel tanquam instrumento
quodam, quo fides hominum, ejusque
constantia probatur, aut in quemcun-
que tandem finem hanc conjunctionem
ipsi permittit. Si enim toties, quoties
ipsi liberet, uti corporibus possfet, ad suam
voluntatem exequendam, nunquam
non abutcretur, imò exiguo tempore
omnia

page.notes: Left and right margins contain fragments of the facing page (partial lines such as "omn", "tam", "lian", "mir", "tue", "per", "qu", "tur", "ext", "pla", "ref" at the right edge) which are cut off and not transcribed. Several words in the scan are blurred, notably "statui posse" and "possfet", and "Genium" in the text may be "Genium" as printed; these are read as printed with low certainty.
